games.note: attempt 1 (superseded, transform spoiled round 2): 20260912-6878, game MRB5P6

round 1 accept branch (kept Grizzly Bears oid 5; rest Forest oid 3 + Duskwatch Recruiter oid 33 to bottom, no ordering choice) and round 2 decline branch (kept 0 of [Recruiter 9, Forest 21, Recruiter 4]; all three to bottom, no ordering choice); pre/post JSON states are from this game

notes: r1 top3 (turn 11): [oid 5 Grizzly Bears, oid 3 Forest, oid 33 Duskwatch Recruiter]; keep select offered the two creatures (selectable_cards [5,33], keep_count 1, up_to true); kept oid 5 -> hand; rest [3,33] landed at library positions 25,26 (the two bottom slots, original relative order).

r2 top3 (turn 13): [oid 9 Duskwatch Recruiter, oid 21 Forest, oid 4 Duskwatch Recruiter]; decline submitted (choiceIds []); rest [9,21,4] landed at positions 23,24,25 (bottom three, original relative order).

Both rounds: engine waiting_for for the keep carried rest_order:'preserve'; after the keep submission the engine returned straight to Priority with no ordering interaction for the rest (A3 failed, A6 failed).
P1's filtered view during both Dig decisions showed all three looked-at cards as 'Hidden Card' (face_down) -- no opponent information leak observed (A5 passed).
P1 cast a 1-mana creature on each of its main phases so 'a spell was cast last turn' stayed true at every P0 upkeep; the Recruiter never transformed in this game.
waiting_for types seen: DeclareAttackers, DigChoice, MulliganDecision, Priority
interaction submissions: keep accept (r1), keep decline (r2), ability activations x2; 0 rejections.

Verdict rationale: the reported defect is the missing controller-selected ordering for the rest ('in any order'). On v0.80.0 the engine offers no ordering choice on either the accept branch or the decline/zero-keep branch and silently preserves the original relative order at the bottom -- exactly the reported behavior, observed twice in one game.
setup_line: P0 (12x Duskwatch Recruiter + Elves/Bears/Forests) vs P1 (12x Llanowar Elves + Forests, casts one each turn to suppress the upkeep transform)
contract_line: After the optional keep, the controller must be able to order every remaining looked-at card; the rest go to the bottom in the submitted order (accept and decline branches)
limitations: Native AI seats not used; the Dig ordering is engine-level and seat-independent
Fewer-than-three-card library edge not exercised (library had 25+ cards)
restoration: pre.json/post.json/pre_r2.json/post_r2.json are authoritative export envelopes ({"state", "precast_shortcut_runtime"}); restored only by inspection in this run, not re-imported into a live game (no ImportAuthoritativeState path used).
